sources.note: Awarding body's own RfRP announcement page on wider.unu.edu (UNU-WIDER's domain). Read in full: background, offer, expectations, evaluation criteria, submission procedure and milestone dates.
UNU-WIDER's own SA-TIED programme page; confirms programme partners (UNU-WIDER, National Treasury, IFPRI) and the tax-data access arrangement.
Live online submission form for individual applicants, still open and accepting entries; restates the deadline and shows the applicant-category options.
Full 'Request for Research Proposals' PDF (Sept 2026), downloaded and text-extracted; identical milestone dates, honorarium terms and eligibility wording to the announcement page.

awarding_body.detail: The page is on wider.unu.edu, the awarding organisation's own domain, and names both UNU-WIDER and the National Treasury of South Africa as the bodies requesting proposals under SA-TIED phase III. Confirmed.
awarding_body.quote: The United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), together with the National Treasury of South Africa (NT), is requesting research proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa – Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme.

deadline.detail: The page states an exact closing date of 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2), with a questions deadline of 8 October 2026 (already passed). Today is 12 October 2026, so the cycle is currently open with three days remaining. The milestone table and the submission form both repeat the same date.

eligibility.detail: All four distinct claims in the record are confirmed verbatim: open to individuals, groups of individuals and non-profit organisations; open to both South Africa-based and international researchers; women, South African researchers, junior/early-career researchers and Global South scholars particularly encouraged or given preference. The call is not restricted by nationality.
eligibility.quote: This call invites South Africa-based and international researchers to submit proposals to conduct research primarily, but not exclusively, using the South African tax administrative data.

funding.detail: The record's funding_type 'Research Funding' is correct. This is not a fully funded scholarship: it is a research honorarium of US$3,000–10,000 paid on delivery of a working paper, plus a small travel stipend for non-Gauteng users of the tax data. No tuition, fees or living costs are covered.
funding.quote: A total research honorarium in the range of US$3,000–10,000 will be paid upon delivery of a working paper, depending on the qualifications of the lead researcher and assessment of the proposal.

degree_levels.detail: The page and the full PDF never state any degree levels or degree-awarding structure — this is a research grant, not a study programme, so 'Postgraduate' is not a claim the page supports or denies. Worse, the live submission form's applicant-category list includes a general 'Student' option alongside 'Professional' and 'Early career researcher (awarded PhD in the last 5 years)', which is at odds with a postgraduate-only reading. Degree levels cannot be confirmed from the page.
degree_levels.quote: I am a Professional Student Early career researcher (awarded PhD in the last 5 years)

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Call closes 15 October 2026 23:59 (UTC+2) — three days after this check, so this record must not be shown as open past that moment. Awarding body, deadline, eligibility wording and the US$3,000–10,000 research honorarium are all confirmed from the UNU-WIDER announcement page, the full RfRP PDF and the live submission form. One claim remains unsupported: the record's degree_levels value 'Postgraduate'. The official pages describe a research grant for 'qualified researchers' and the submission form explicitly offers 'Professional', 'Student' and 'Early career researcher (awarded PhD in the last 5 years)' as applicant categories, so a postgraduate-only degree level is not evidenced. Reviewers should either change degree_levels to a value reflecting a non-degree research grant (e.g. 'Not a degree programme - research grant for qualified researchers') or mark it as unspecified. Questions deadline (8 Oct 2026) has already passed.

notes_for_reviewer: Two things a human must decide. (1) Degree levels: the record says 'Postgraduate' but the official pages never state degree levels, and the live submission form admits a plain 'Student' category; the value looks like an editorial inference rather than something the awarding body states. This is the sole reason the verdict is needs_review rather than active — everything else checks out cleanly. (2) Time-sensitivity: the cycle closes at 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026, which is three days after this check, so whichever status is applied, the record needs an automated flip to closed/expired on 16 October 2026; the same SA-TIED RfRP will likely be re-issued for a later cycle, at which point the deadline fields will need re-checking.
